headline: Highest risk is medium: ComfyUI can ingest files and model assets, but awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O, so pairwise interaction is limited and mostly indirect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction channel exists between awesome-selfhosted and ComfyUI. Profile A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; profile B has filesystem inputs but no shared channel, clipboard, or MCP bridge to ingest A’s content as instructions.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies text from awesome-selfhosted into a ComfyUI prompt or workflow node, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the list and ComfyUI in separate windows/workspaces.
Do not paste repository text into ComfyUI prompts or nodes.
Use a read-only browser for the list and a separate editor for workflows.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and cannot run, while ComfyUI is local/offline by default and only egresses to vendor services. There is no documented shared workspace or shared principal, so leakage between them is not established; the main risk is accidental manual transfer of sensitive prompts or assets.
conditions: IF the operator stores sensitive images or prompts in files that ComfyUI loads, those contents may be exposed to its local workflow and any vendor API use.
mitigations: Keep sensitive assets in a separate directory.
Disable any vendor API calls not needed for the task.
Review loaded workflow files before execution.
Use non-sensitive test images for validation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend with ComfyUI over mutable resources. ComfyUI also cannot write files or modify git state, and supports only one instance, so there is no overlapping write surface to conflict over.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid sharing a mutable working directory.
Run ComfyUI in a dedicated folder.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge list, not an action-taking agent, so it cannot authoritatively drive ComfyUI. ComfyUI can consume workflows and assets, but the pair lacks a documented pipeline where A’s output is automatically treated as authoritative input by B, making cascading error mainly a manual workflow risk.
conditions: IF an operator converts entries from awesome-selfhosted into ComfyUI workflows without verification, incorrect configuration can propagate.
mitigations: Verify any copied workflow settings against upstream docs.
Use a second person or checklist for workflow changes.
Test new workflows on a non-production image first.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. awesome-selfhosted touches no regulated data classes, and ComfyUI’s documented data classes are media/model artifacts rather than PHI or residency-bound records. Without a shared regulated data flow, the compliance pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into ComfyUI workflows, compliance review would be required.
mitigations: Avoid loading regulated data into ComfyUI.
Document any data-class changes before deployment.
Keep workflow assets non-sensitive by default.
